discovery: Quantum control of macroscopic mechanical oscillators: ground-state preparation and quantum-coherent manipulation of engineered mechanical motion

nominees.name: Markus Aspelmeyer
nominees.affiliation: University of Vienna and IQOQI Vienna, Austria

nominees.name: Andrew N. Cleland
nominees.affiliation: Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering, University of Chicago, USA

nominees.name: John D. Teufel
nominees.affiliation: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Boulder, USA

subfield: Quantum optics / cavity and circuit optomechanics
motivation: For decades, mechanical objects visible to the eye were assumed to behave purely classically. The nominees overturned this. Cleland (2010) placed a macroscopic piezoelectric resonator in its quantum ground state and controlled single phonons by coupling it to a superconducting qubit. Teufel (2011) used radiation-pressure sideband cooling in a microwave circuit to cool a drumhead to its ground state, then entangled mechanical motion with microwave fields. Aspelmeyer pioneered optomechanical strong coupling, quantum-coherent optical control of mechanical motion, and the ground-state cooling of levitated nanoparticles, opening tests of quantum mechanics and gravity with massive objects. Together they established engineered mechanical oscillators as a quantum system on a par with atoms, ions and superconducting circuits. This enables measurements beyond the standard quantum limit, quantum transduction between microwave and optical photons, and new probes of fundamental physics.
